function: Meta-SAC jointly learns BS beamforming vectors, STAR-BD-RIS scattering matrices, and BS antenna selection to maximize energy efficiency (pp. 1, 3).
system: BS with 4 antennas, 2 STAR-BD-RISs (cell-wise single-connected, 4 antennas per sector), 8 single-antenna users, flat fading; band not stated (pp. 2, 4).
method: Soft actor-critic with meta-critic meta-learning (reinforcement), hybrid constraint-penalty reward with learnable weights, replay buffer, 6000 episodes (pp. 3-4, Table I).
data_channel: Own simulator: flat-fading Rician channels (LOS plus Gaussian NLOS), path-loss exponent 2, random user positions; deterministic coefficients in learning curves; perfect CSI (pp. 2, 4).
test_conditions: One simulated setting for training and evaluation; sweeps of the number of users (2-8) and of RIS elements (4-36); no test on unseen conditions (pp. 4-5).
baselines: Learned: Meta-DDPG and Meta-TD3 (other meta-DRL algorithms). Non-learned: convex optimization (SDP/SCA). System benchmarks: single STAR-BD-RIS, conventional RIS, no RIS (pp. 4-5).
metrics: Energy efficiency (bps/Joule/Hz), total rate R_T, total power P_T and reward versus episodes; EE versus number of users and RIS elements (pp. 4-5).
complexity: Order O(sum of neuron products over actor, critic, meta-critic layers); convex benchmark order also given; no measured runtime (pp. 4-5).
q1_support: p. 2: "denote the path loss exponent and the Rician factors". The channels are an own LOS plus Gaussian NLOS flat-fading model (p. 2); no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, or measured data is named.
q2_support: p. 4: "Then, a mini-batch of Bval is sampled from the replay buffer." Training and validation batches of the meta step come from the same replay buffer (Algorithm 1); the paper reports no test on an unseen scenario and no adaptation, and Figs. 4-5 sweeps are not stated to reuse a trained agent.
q3_support: p. 5: "we compared it with the convex optimization approach" (EE, Fig. 4) and "Fig. 5 compares EE obtained in multi-STAR-BD-RIS with other meta DRL algorithms" (legends of Figs. 3-5: Meta-DDPG, Meta-TD3).
q4_support: p. 4: "where U , P, and W denote the number of actor, critic, and meta-critic layers, respectively." The order of Meta-SAC is a sum of neuron products over these layers (Section IV-A); p. 5 gives the order of the convex benchmark.
q5_support: p. 4: "all users are located in a circle according to uniform random distribution". The data come from the authors' own simulator; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset or measurements.
notes: Included in area 3: Meta-SAC learns BS beamforming, STAR-BD-RIS matrices and antenna selection (p. 3, action space), all physical-layer decisions. The meta-learning is a meta-critic inside a single environment (Algorithm 1, p. 4), not adaptation to new tasks, so q2 is 0. q3: convex optimization is the non-learned baseline (Fig. 4); Meta-DDPG and Meta-TD3 are other DRL algorithms (DDPG, TD3) with a meta-critic, which the reviewer may confirm are not variants of the proposal. Table I (p. 4) and the legends of Figs. 3-5 (p. 5) were read from the page images because the text extraction omits them.
